systemPrompt:
You create original generative art and animations for Canvas using p5.js 1.9 global mode.
Always write a complete custom sketch, not a template selection. Return ONLY valid JSON:
{"title":"Short artwork title","code":"complete JavaScript","params":[{"id":"speed","name":"Speed","type":"number","default":1,"min":0,"max":4,"step":0.1}]}

Declare 3–6 useful controls in params. Supported types:
- number: finite min < max, positive step, default within bounds
- color: default is a six-digit HEX string, e.g. "#ff6699"
- boolean: default is true or false
- enum: options is a nonempty array of strings, default is one of those strings
Each control needs a unique JavaScript identifier id and a short human-readable name.
Do not use code, constructor, prototype, or __proto__ as control ids.

Runtime contract:
- The host provides a mutable global object called params, initialized with your control defaults.
- Read params.speed, params.color, etc. directly in draw(), not only during setup(). Never declare or shadow params.
- EVERY declared control must visibly affect the artwork when changed, without reloading or resetting animation.
- For counts, initialize enough elements for the maximum and draw only the current count, or reconcile counts in draw().
- Define function setup() and function draw(). setup() calls createCanvas(windowWidth, windowHeight).
- Define function windowResized() { resizeCanvas(windowWidth, windowHeight); }.
- Do not use new p5(), HTML, imports, external libraries, network calls, or DOM controls.
- Call p5 functions only inside setup/draw/events, not at top level. The host seeds random and noise before setup.
- Keep the code focused and complete so it fits the response budget. No markdown fences.

When editing, preserve the current composition and existing controls unless the request needs a change.
The control defaults in your response must reflect the requested changes and the current values.
Return the full code and full control list on every request.

Curated style references (inspiration only, not output template ids):
Particle System: A swarm of particles moving organically with mouse attraction.
Noise Flow Field: Smooth flowing lines driven by Perlin noise.
Geometric Grid: Structured grid with random geometric shapes.
Brush Playground: Expressive brush strokes that follow the mouse.
Radial Mandala: Symmetrical radial patterns with layered geometry.
Typography Warp: Text distorted by sine waves.
3D Geometry (WEBGL): Explore 3D space, lighting, and materials.
Recursive Fractal Tree: A mathematical tree generated using recursive functions and transformations.
Lissajous Curves: Complex harmonic motion created with trigonometry.
Bouncing Balls: Physics simulation with gravity, bouncing, and collisions.
Flocking Boids: Emergent flocking behavior using Craig Reynolds boids algorithm.
Game of Life: Conway's Game of Life cellular automaton simulation.
Meta-balls: Organic blob-like isosurfaces using marching squares.
3D Terrain (WEBGL): Procedural 3D terrain generated from Perlin noise, rendered in WebGL.
Spirograph: Mathematical spirograph curves using parametric equations.
Fireworks: Exploding particle fireworks with gravity and trail effects.
Kaleidoscope: Interactive kaleidoscope drawing tool with mirror symmetry.
Color Waves: Animated flowing color gradients using sine waves and color interpolation.
Rain: Atmospheric rain effect with wind, splashes, and layered depth.
Neon Lines: Particles connected by glowing lines when close to each other.
Truchet Tiles: Procedural tiling patterns using Truchet tile arrangements.
Wave Interference: Simulation of overlapping waves creating interference patterns.
Reaction-Diffusion: Gray-Scott reaction-diffusion system producing organic patterns.
Solar System: 2D orbital mechanics simulation with planets orbiting a star.
Audio Visualizer: Sound-reactive visualization using p5.sound FFT analysis. Enable mic or use the built-in oscillator.
Virtual Aquarium: Mic-reactive migration sim — small fish flee sound, big fish hunt toward it.
Interactive Playground: Multi-input interactive sketch responding to mouse, keyboard, and webcam motion.
Video Feedback: Webcam capture with real-time pixel effects, feedback loops, and glitch aesthetics.
Phyllotaxis: Fibonacci spiral pattern found in sunflowers and pinecones.
Circle Packing: Circles that grow and pack together without overlapping.
Maze Generator: DFS recursive backtracking maze generation with animated solving.
Double Pendulum: Chaotic motion of a double pendulum with trail visualization.
Fluid Ripple: 2D water ripple simulation using wave propagation algorithm.
L-System: Formal grammar fractal plant growth using Lindenmayer systems.
DLA Crystal Growth: Diffusion-limited aggregation — organic crystal/dendrite formation.
Sorting Visualizer: Animated visualization of classic sorting algorithms.
Isometric Cubes: 3D isometric cube projection rendered on 2D canvas.
Worley Noise: Cellular noise texture based on distance to random feature points.
Dithering: Floyd-Steinberg error diffusion dithering on procedural patterns.
Maurer Rose: Mathematical rose curves with rotating line segments.
Gradient Mesh: Smooth color gradient mesh with animated control points.
Drip Effect: Paint dripping and splatter effect with fluid physics.
Swirl: Hypnotic conical swirl pattern with color distortion.
Halftone: Halftone dot pattern effect on procedural shapes.
Pixel Sort: Glitchy pixel sorting effect on procedural gradients.
ASCII Render: Live canvas rendered as ASCII text art.
Chain Reaction: Abelian sandpile model — self-organized criticality simulation.
Voronoi Diagram: Voronoi tessellation with animated site points and colored cells.
Lorenz Attractor: 3D strange attractor visualization of the Lorenz chaotic system.
Spring System: Mass-spring physics simulation with connected particles and tension.
notes: 32 distinct creation prompts; no editing context. Actual app schema/syntax validator and generated HTML in Chromium; 2.5-second default-state smoke test, no control mutation or visual fidelity scoring. Costs not independently verified. No retries.

{
  "title": "Seasonal Fractal Tree",
  "code": "let maxDepth = 10;\nfunction setup() {\n  createCanvas(windowWidth, windowHeight);\n  angleMode(RADIANS);\n}\nfunction draw() {\n  background(params.bgColor);\n  let baseColor;\n  let leafColor;\n  if (params.season === \"Spring\") {\n    baseColor = color(100, 70, 40);\n    leafColor = color(255, 150, 180, 200);\n  } else if (params.season === \"Summer\") {\n    baseColor = color(80, 50, 30);\n    leafColor = color(50, 200, 80, 200);\n  } else if (params.season === \"Autumn\") {\n    baseColor = color(90, 60, 40);\n    leafColor = color(230, 120, 30, 200);\n  } else {\n    baseColor = color(60, 60, 70);\n    leafColor = color(220, 230, 255, 180);\n  }\n  push();\n  translate(width / 2, height - 50);\n  let len = height * 0.22;\n  stroke(baseColor);\n  strokeWeight(params.trunkWidth);\n  branch(len, 0, baseColor, leafColor);\n  pop();\n}\nfunction branch(len, depth, baseColor, leafColor) {\n  let angleSway = sin(frameCount * 0.02 * params.speed + depth * 0.5) * 0.05 * params.wind;\n  let theta = params.branchAngle + angleSway;\n  line(0, 0, 0, -len);\n  translate(0, -len);\n  if (depth < params.depth) {\n    push();\n    rotate(theta);\n    strokeWeight(max(0.5, params.trunkWidth * pow(0.7, depth + 1)));\n    branch(len * params.lengthRatio, depth + 1, baseColor, leafColor);\n    pop();\n\n    push();\n    rotate(-theta);\n    strokeWeight(max(0.5, params.trunkWidth * pow(0.7, depth + 1)));\n    branch(len * params.lengthRatio, depth + 1, baseColor, leafColor);\n    pop();\n  } else {\n    noStroke();\n    fill(leafColor);\n    ellipse(0, 0, params.leafSize, params.leafSize * 1.5);\n  }\n}\nfunction windowResized() {\n  resizeCanvas(windowWidth, windowHeight);\n}",

{
  "title": "Lorenz Attractor",
  "code": "let points = [];\nlet x = 0.01;\nlet y = 0;\nlet z = 0;\nlet sigma = 10;\nlet rho = 28;\nlet beta = 8.0 / 3.0;\nlet angle = 0;\n\nfunction setup() {\n  createCanvas(windowWidth, windowHeight, WEBGL);\n  colorMode(HSB, 360, 100, 100, 100);\n  x = 0.01;\n  y = 0;\n  z = 0;\n  points = [];\n}\n\nfunction draw() {\n  background(params.bgHue, 40, 15);\n\n  let dt = 0.01 * params.speed;\n  let stepsPerFrame = floor(params.detail);\n\n  for (let s = 0; s < stepsPerFrame; s++) {\n    let dx = (sigma * (y - x)) * dt;\n    let dy = (x * (rho - z) - y) * dt;\n    let dz = (x * y - beta * z) * dt;\n    x += dx;\n    y += dy;\n    z += dz;\n    points.push(createVector(x, y, z));\n\n    let maxPoints = floor(params.length);\n    if (points.length > maxPoints) {\n      points.shift();\n    }\n  }\n\n  rotateX(frameCount * 0.002 * params.rotSpeed);\n  rotateY(angle);\n  angle += 0.005 * params.rotSpeed;\n\n  scale(params.scaleFactor);\n  translate(0, 0, -80);\n\n  noFill();\n  beginShape();\n  for (let i = 0; i < points.length; i++) {\n    let p = points[i];\n    let hueVal = (params.startHue + (i / points.length) * 180) % 360;\n    stroke(hueVal, 80, 90, 80);\n    strokeWeight(params.weight);\n    vertex(p.x, p.y, p.z);\n  }\n  endShape();\n}\n\nfunction windowResized() {\n  resizeCanvas(windowWidth, windowHeight);\n}",
